What was basic training like? I've seen several videos on Youtube depicting a pretty strict and abusive environment in Russia. Given these are probably abnormal and I'm sure you will find this kind of hazing anywhere but I'm curious to hear it from someone that went through it. Thanks for doing this!

Thanks for the question, have an upvoat.

Basic training was pretty exhausting, both physically and mentally, though, to be honest, after a certain point you just stop caring, anything they throw at you becomes "just another day at the job". The environment is extremely abusive, but you get desensitized to it very quickly, unless you are psychologically weak.
How long were you in the service?
Thanks for the question! Have an upvoat. Two years.
Were you involved in the Moscow Theater attack? What are your thoughts on using gas attacks on local populations?
I was not. I personally am completely against it, we've trained with this gas and we are fully aware of how dangerous it is. In the case of that attack they had to use it as a last resort.
Worst thing to happen to us since Stalin.
How are living conditions in the Russian army? Are elites treated differently than the drafted?

We do get a bit better accommodations and food, but the treatment is much more strict. Normal Russian draftee regiments are pretty lax as long as you do a certain minimum of things. In our case, however, our entire day was very heavily controlled all the time by officers.
I'm pretty sure if there is ever war, there will not be an invasion.

What are some of the methods your commanding officers used to punish insubordination?

On an related note: What are your thoughts on the Roman Military tactic of Decimation?

The main method of punishment would be group punishment. Very rarely would officers punish individual soldiers. If one of us fucked up, his entire squad would be punished. It's supposed to be a way of team building but in reality all it did was create hostility between us. And the officers would more often than not abuse their powers.

I think it's a waste of life.
